findings: openhcl/underhill_core/src/worker.rs:2220-2233 calls isolated-configuration validation on cold initialization.
worker.rs:4084-4085 explicitly rejects hibernation_enabled for isolated configurations.
Host-side Save-VM is refused for this VM isolation type.
Native app lifecycle supports start/stop; it owns no guest CPU/RAM checkpoint primitive.
No isolation gate was bypassed, no diagnostic VM was started, and the running native desktop was not modified.
The Linux userspace snapshot path with platform_support=false does not use ACPI S4 callbacks; OpenHCL host-hibernation rejection alone does not prove it impossible.
Native owner source audit found no blanket gate in that path, but the custom TPM control-page mapping lacks restore callbacks and requires re-registration plus fresh attestation.
decision: Continue qualifying a guest-managed checkpoint on the existing isolation platform. Earlier platform-replacement question was premature.
